To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The training goals for the three training courses we studied (the two courses on software development and the one course on software maintenance) were not stated in a form that would allow the evaluation of training effectiveness, 2) The evaluation goals for these training courses were stated in a form such that they would allow the evaluation only of training effectiveness in a limited way, 3) The evaluation goals were not stated with sufficient clarity to guide the selection of evaluation methods, and 4) The

(1) training evaluation is feasible in underresourced contexts and (2) a comprehensive approach to managing training evaluation, including formative, intrinsic, and pay-off evaluation methods, can be successfully implemented.
• The use of a training evaluation framework that incorporates both formative and summulative evaluation is feasible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a framework to guide the evaluation of training systems, particularly those developed to support the acquisition of complex skills.
the design and implementation of methods of evaluation.
the development of a framework for managing evaluation in the context of a training program.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

intrinsic evaluation methods are the most appropriate when the purpose of the evaluation is to determine the effectiveness of a program in terms of the extent to which it achieves the objectives that were set for it; and extrinsic methods are the most suitable when the purpose of an evaluation is to determine whether the program is achieving its objectives in terms of some other criteria.
intrinsic methods are those that evaluate a design on its own terms, and pay-off methods are those that relate the design to some external criterion.
formative evaluation methods are intrinsic and summative evaluation methods are pay-off methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a framework for managing the goals of training evaluation in the context of training for the use of complex information systems.
intrinsic methods are more useful for formative evaluation, while pay-off methods are more useful to support summative evaluation.

the intrinsic evaluation method is a method of evaluating the design of an instructional system, and the pay-off method is a method for evaluating the effectiveness of an instructional system. (p. 5) Intrinsic evaluation methods seek to assess a design product in its own terms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
training evaluation should be a continuous process, not an event.
the evaluation process can be used to help the organization understand the value of the training program and the return on its investment.
the training evaluation literature has been dominated by the intrinsic approach, with the pay-off approach receiving relatively little attention.
